summary.text: A 62-year-old man with treatment-resistant bipolar II depression and hypertension had a first major depressive episode in 2004, a hypomanic episode in 2005 and retirement in 2012 after prolonged low mood. Second and third major depressive episodes in 2017 and 2019 each involved a suicide attempt, and a fourth episode occurred in 2022.

Multiple psychotropic drugs, including venlafaxine, mirtazapine, lithium, olanzapine and quetiapine, produced a poor response. ECT with intravenous ketamine in 2019 (12 sessions) gave partial improvement, and rTMS for 2 years gave only a partial response; ECT and rTMS were later refused.

CTA was performed before starting esketamine nasal spray in October 2022. First induction was twice weekly for 4 weeks with venlafaxine, mirtazapine, lithium and quetiapine; PHQ-9 fell from 25 to 15, then to 7 by March 2023 and 5 by July 2023 during weekly, biweekly and monthly maintenance, with near-remission.

A buying spree occurred during monthly dosing without other manic symptoms and did not meet hypomanic or manic criteria. In July 2023 the dosing interval was extended to once every 2 months and lithium was raised from 300 mg every other day to 300 mg daily. Depression recurred in December 2023 with PHQ-9 23; a 1-month second induction brought PHQ-9 to 12, then 8 by April 2024 and 6 in July 2024.

Throughout treatment he had dissociation, dizziness and transient hypertension; elevated BP followed each administration and subsided quickly. On regular nebivolol and valsartan with usual BP below 130 mm Hg, SBP exceeded 160 mm Hg on three occasions with dizziness and headaches and nifedipine was given; no other complications were noted. The authors recommend dosing at least once every 4 weeks.

caption_evidence.quote:
Figure 1.
Bipolar life chart. The vertical axis represents mood severity, while the horizontal axis represents duration and time. The patient experienced one hypomanic episode in 2005 and five major depressive episodes in 2004, 2017, 2019, 2022, and 2024, respectively. He underwent electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) with intravenous ketamine in 2019 and received repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (rTMS) for 2 years (2020–2022). Esketamine nasal spray (ESK-NS) treatment began in October 2022, with clinical improvement observed most of the time. Buying sprees were noted in July 2023 but did not meet the criteria for a hypomanic or manic episode. The fifth depressive episode was noted when the interval of ESK-NS was adjusted to once every 2 months in 2024.
